title: Saw a 45-degree mitre on a picture-frame moulding in a mitre box, one hand holding the moulding to the fence
instruction: Cut the mitre: lay the moulding in the mitre box against its back fence with the pencil line at the 45-degree slot, and hold it there with one hand. With the other take the backsaw from its rest, set it in that 45-degree slot and saw back and forth until the moulding is cut through. Then stand the saw back in its rest, lift the cut moulding out of the box onto the table in front of it, and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Picture framers and carpenters cut mitred corners in a mitre box: the moulding is held against the back fence with one hand while the other works the backsaw in the angled slot, since the saw's strokes drag the moulding along otherwise.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A brown beech mitre box, fixed: a plywood base board 1.5 cm thick, from 29.7 to 40.3 cm forward and from 15 cm right to 28 cm left of the centre line, and on it a front wall and a back fence, each 1.5 cm thick and 5 cm tall, running from 15 cm right to 8 cm left, with a 6 cm wide channel between them (its back fence's face 38 cm forward). Saw slots cut through both walls: two at 45 degrees crossing the channel's middle 5 cm right of the centre line, and one at 90 degrees 3 cm left of it. (2) On the table in front of the box, a length of black-lacquered picture-frame moulding (94 g), 34 cm long, 2.6 cm wide and 2.2 cm tall, with a gold lip along its front edge, lying along the box 21.5 cm forward, from 8.3 cm right to 25.7 cm left of the centre line; a white pencil line crosses its top at 45 degrees 5 cm from its right end. (3) To the right, a backsaw (160 g): a steel blade 24 cm long and 5 cm deep with a brass back and a turned rosewood handle in line with it, standing teeth down in a beech saw rest (two V-blocks under the blade and a V-cradle under the handle) 21 cm right of the centre line, the blade running forward from 26 to 50 cm, the handle reaching back toward the arms. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged from the whole trial. The moulding is at the mark when its pencil line lies within 1 cm of the 45-degree slot along the box, its back face within 6 mm of the fence, turned less than 4 degrees and lying on the box's floor; it has been laid there once it stays so for 0.5 s. The saw is in the slot when it is turned within 8 degrees of the slot, leans less than 12 degrees, lies within 9 mm of the slot's line and its teeth rest on the bottom of the cut (within 7 mm above and 8 mm below it). A stroke: the saw, in the slot, pushed 3 cm along it while the moulding lies at the mark and moves no more than 4 mm; each stroke deepens the cut 2.9 mm, and after eight the moulding is cut through. The saw is back in its rest when it stands within 2 cm of where it started, within 1.2 cm of its height and turned less than 10 degrees from it; the cut moulding is out on the table when it lies on the table in front of the box's base board. 1.0: cut through, the saw back in its rest, the cut moulding out on the table and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start), at the end; 0.75: cut through; 0.5: at least four strokes; 0.25: the moulding laid at the mark; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the saw and both pieces of the moulding still.
reset_notes: Lay the moulding back in one piece on the table in front of the box, and stand the saw back in its rest, teeth down, handle toward the arms.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the wood is not cut; strokes are counted by a rule, and the saw's teeth ride on a hidden plate inside the moulding that steps down with each stroke and drags the moulding along by friction. A fixed joint holds the two pieces together until the cut is through. The saw's weight sits near its handle. The box and the rest are fixed. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
